The Cambrian and West Valley areas have nine high schools and are divided into four elementary school districts containing seventy-eight elementary schools. In addition, the Santa Clara Unified District serves Alvosi and a very small portion of city residents in the North San Jose Planning Area. Although district boundaries are very broad, most of the schools are located within the San Jose corporate limits. The Alum Rock area is served by the Eastside Union District and the Central area is within the boundaries of the Campbell Union and San Jose Unified districts.
Recently many County school districts have expereinced diminishing enrollments as area-wide demographic changes occur. Table <u>VI</u> on the following page shows the 1976 and 1977 school enrollments for districts in San Jose and the percentage of student loss or gain.
Park Facilities
For park planning purposes, the city categorizes park sites by their size and nature of development into three types of facilities: Neighborhood parks, district parks, and city-wide parks. They are generally defined in accordance with the following criteria:
Nieghborhood Parks:
These are normally six to eight acres in size and located to serve 4,000 to 6,000 people in geographically distinct neighborhoods. Seventy-nine neighborhood parks are maintained by the City on 499.5 acres. (53 developed; 369.1 acres)
District Parks:
The average size of existing district parks is approximately 18 acres. They are located geographically to serve from 16,000 to 30,000 people within a radium of approximately 1.5 miles. The City has ten such facilities on 141.8 acres. (10 developed; 101.2 acres)
City-Wide Parks:
As the name denotes, these serve the entire City. Features may include a variety of special use facilities and development consistent with the geographical and environmental character stics of the site for use by large numbers of City residents. Theere are sixteen of these sites encompassing a toal of 1,503.5 acres. (5 developed: 243.2 acres). In addition, the City has 23 mini-parks (less than two acres) with a total of 13.6 acres (13 developed; 48 acres).
